$comment: Advisories accepted after assessing exposure in this application.
Each entry needs a reason and a reviewOn date. An expired entry fails the
build, so accepted risk gets revisited instead of quietly accumulating.
Anything not listed here still fails CI at high severity.

allow.reason: Reaches us through the Prisma CLI, which is a development and migration tool. It is not installed in either production image, and the stack-exhaustion path needs a recursive object graph we never hand it.

mysql2 is bundled inside the Prisma CLI, which supports several database engines. This project's datasource provider is postgresql and no MySQL connection is ever opened, so the auth-plugin downgrade cannot be reached: it requires connecting to a hostile MySQL server. The CLI is a build and migration tool and is excluded from both production images.
Same bundled Prisma CLI dependency. The decompression bomb needs a MySQL server speaking the compressed protocol, and this project never connects to MySQL.
